units.text: Android apps need to adapt to many changing conditions: window sizes, locales, font sizes, dark and light themes, and more. Testing different configurations directly in a test is difficult since the test must configure device-level properties.

quotes.quote: Android apps need to adapt to many changing conditions: window sizes, locales, font sizes, dark and light themes, and more.
Testing different configurations directly in a test is difficult since the test must configure device-level properties.

units.text: `DeviceConfigurationOverride` is a test-only API that lets you simulate different device configurations in a localized way for the `@Composable` content under test.

quotes.quote: is a test-only API that lets you simulate different device configurations in a localized way for the @Composable content under test.

units.text: The release notes for 1.7.0-alpha01 say: adds `DeviceConfigurationOverride` API to `ui-test` to allow locally overriding the behavior of content under test, such as to specify an available size, locale, layout direction, font scale, or theme.

quotes.quote: Adds DeviceConfigurationOverride API to ui-test to allow locally overriding the behavior of content under test, such as to specify an available size, locale, layout direction, font scale, or theme.

units.text: The companion object of `DeviceConfigurationOverride` has the following extension functions, which override device-level configuration properties:

quotes.quote: The companion object of DeviceConfigurationOverride has the following extension functions, which override device-level configuration properties:

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.DarkMode()`: Overrides the system to dark theme or light theme.

quotes.quote: Overrides the system to dark theme or light theme.

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.FontScale()`: Overrides the system font scale.

quotes.quote: Overrides the system font scale.

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.FontWeightAdjustment()`: Overrides the system font weight adjustment.

quotes.quote: Overrides the system font weight adjustment.

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.ForcedSize()`: Forces a specific amount of space regardless of device size.

quotes.quote: Forces a specific amount of space regardless of device size.

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.LayoutDirection()`: Overrides the layout direction (left-to-right or right-to-left).

quotes.quote: Overrides the layout direction (left-to-right or right-to-left).

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.Locales()`: Overrides the locale.

quotes.quote: Overrides the locale.

units.text: - `DeviceConfigurationOverride.RoundScreen()`: Overrides if the screen is round.

quotes.quote: Overrides if the screen is round.

units.text: Specifying a resource qualifier is quite simple: simply add the desired qualifiers to the `@Config` annotation on your test case or test class, depending on whether you would like to change the resource qualifiers for the whole file, or simply one test.

For example, qualifiers at the test method level occlude qualifiers at the test class level. However, if the qualifiers config property starts with a + (plus sign), it is interpreted as an overlay to any higher-level qualifiers that have been specified:

units.text: `ActivityController.configurationChange()` can be used to simulate the sequence of events that take place on a device when its configuration changes. If the Activity is configured to handle the configuration changes, `ActivityController.configurationChange()` will call the Activity's `onConfigurationChanged()` method. If not, `ActivityController` destroys and recreates the Activity.

quotes.quote: ActivityController.configurationChange() can be used to simulate the sequence of events that take place on a device when its configuration changes. If the Activity is configured to handle the configuration changes, ActivityController.configurationChange() will call the Activity's onConfigurationChanged() method. If not, ActivityController destroys and recreates the Activity.

units.text: Robolectric allows display properties to be changed during a test using setters on `ShadowDisplay`. Multiple displays can be simulated using APIs on `ShadowDisplayManager`.

quotes.quote: Robolectric allows display properties to be changed during a test using setters on ShadowDisplay. Multiple displays can be simulated using APIs on ShadowDisplayManager.

units.text: The AndroidX Test page on Robolectric.org says Robolectric provides `Robolectric.setupActivity()` for the coarse-grained use case where you require a launched activity in the resumed state and visible for the user to interact with, and `Robolectric.buildActivity()`, which returns an `ActivityController` that allows the developer to step through the Activity lifecycle. It says `buildActivity()` has proved problematic as it requires developers to fully understand valid lifecycle transitions and possible valid states, and that `ActivityScenario` provides a replacement for both of these use cases, but places tighter restrictions around lifecycle transitions, namely that invalid or incomplete transitions are not possible.

quotes.quote: Robolectric provides Robolectric.setupActivity() for the coarse-grained use case where you require a launched activity in the resumed state and visible for the user to interact with.

Robolectric also provides Robolectric.buildActivity(), which returns an ActivityController that allows the developer to step through the Activity lifecycle. This has proved problematic as it requires developers to fully understand valid lifecycle transitions and possible valid states.
ActivityScenario provides a replacement for both of these use cases, but places tighter restrictions around lifecycle transitions, namely that invalid or incomplete transitions are not possible.

units.text: A Robolectric blog post that calls itself an outside read of the code, not an official AndroidX position, says of `window-testing` that the fakes are pure JUnit and that Robolectric only provides the JVM Android types (`Rect`, `WindowLayoutInfo`) so the tests can build them off-device.

quotes.quote: This is an outside read of the code as it stands in mid-2026, not an official AndroidX position
The fakes are pure JUnit; Robolectric only provides the JVM Android types (Rect, WindowLayoutInfo) so the tests can build them off-device.
